spec.question: Does severe subordinate phenotype drift require a persistent identity primitive, or are observable dependency/currentness plus subsequent actual outcomes sufficient?
spec.incumbent: Higher-level request-effect knowledge should stale only when an owned observable premise changes; hidden subordinate phenotype change with unchanged qualified request-channel premises is not pre-observably identifiable and should be corrected by subsequent actual outcomes.
spec.rival: A persistent subordinate identity/phenotype owner is required to invalidate higher-level relations before any changed outcome is observed.
spec.manipulation: Learn a parent request-effect relation against subordinate V1. Replace the subordinate with V2 while preserving outward request handle metadata in one condition and changing capability epoch/signature in another; independently vary whether V2 preserves or changes actual request consequence.
controls: explicit request-channel epoch/signature drift positive stale control
spec.incumbent_prediction: Explicit observable dependency drift stales immediately; hidden effect-preserving swap does not; hidden effect-changing swap remains provisionally current until actual outcome evidence updates/demotes it. No identity primitive is needed.
spec.rival_prediction: Any severe phenotype replacement must invalidate/reidentify the relation before outcome contact even when all owned observable premises are identical.
spec.measurement: Relation current/stale status before first post-swap outcome, request selection, actual outcome, learned relation update after outcome, restart behavior.
spec.minimal_embodiment: Two-level hierarchy fixture only; swap subordinate handlers/state mappings without production changes.
spec.falsifier: A hidden phenotype change that is observationally identical to current owners causes lawful pre-outcome invalidation via an existing non-identity dependency, or currentness fails to stale when an explicitly owned dependency changes.
spec.loop_plus: If divergence exists, audit whether an omitted operational dependency—not numerical identity—explains it.
